factors.name: Accelerating SBC Dilution Supply Drift
factors.description: Construct a negative cross-sectional score from the quarterly change in stockBasedCompensation-to-revenue, sharesGrowth, netStockIssuance scaled by marketCap, and the gap between stockBasedCompensation and the absolute value of shareRepurchase. Use sector-relative ranks and attenuate observations with missing or stale share-count data.
factors.trading_idea: Stock-based compensation creates a predictable future share-supply overhang that is often obscured by adjusted earnings and only gradually incorporated by discretionary investors. Short firms with rising SBC intensity, positive share-count growth, and net stock issuance, particularly when buybacks are insufficient to offset issuance; buy the converse. This mechanism is falsified if subsequent returns do not worsen as dilution acceleration increases after controlling for profitability and size, since the anticipated issuance would then already be priced.

factors.name: Cash-Quality-Confirmed Surprise Drift
factors.description: On fresh EPS-surprise updates, the factor multiplies the cross-sectional surprise rank by the centered cross-sectional rank of income quality. It is positive for good surprises with strong cash backing and bad surprises with weak cash backing, and is inactive outside the report-information window.
factors.trading_idea: Earnings surprises should drift when reported earnings are corroborated by operating cash generation, because investors initially focus on the headline surprise and process its persistence more gradually. Positive surprises paired with high income quality are more likely to represent durable operating improvement, while negative surprises paired with weak income quality are more likely to signal genuine deterioration. This refinement removes several fragile cash-flow subcomponents and the short-window price-reaction gate, retaining the core delayed-validation mechanism in a sign-consistent form.

factors.name: Fresh Cash-Flow-Confirmed Surprise Drift
factors.description: Detects new EPS or revenue-surprise disclosures, scales their signed cross-sectional surprise strength by a cash-flow credibility score, and ranks the resulting fresh-event signal. Credibility combines income quality, free-cash-flow yield, and quarter-over-quarter cash-conversion-cycle improvement.
factors.trading_idea: Post-earnings drift should be concentrated immediately after a newly disclosed estimate surprise, rather than being repeatedly traded while quarterly surprise fields are forward-filled. A positive surprise is more credible when operating earnings convert into cash, free-cash-flow support is strong, and the cash-conversion cycle is not deteriorating; those events should attract sustained analyst and institutional reassessment over the following week. The refinement therefore treats cash-flow quality as a contemporaneous credibility condition on fresh earnings news, not as a persistent standalone valuation signal.

factors.name: Cash-Backed Asymmetric Surprise Drift
factors.description: Ranks a bounded EPS-surprise intensity cross-sectionally, then applies a sign-aware income-quality confirmation adjustment. The signal is active only for six bars following a newly available EPS-surprise report.
factors.trading_idea: Earnings-surprise drift should be strongest when the surprise direction is corroborated by the reported cash-conversion quality of earnings. The prior implementation accidentally discarded the surprise direction by multiplying two centered ranks, which can score negative surprises with weak quality as positive. This refinement preserves surprise sign while asymmetrically amplifying positive surprises with strong cash support and negative surprises with weak or negative cash support, focusing only on the immediate post-report assimilation window.

factors.name: Fresh Cash-Realization Surprise Disagreement
factors.description: Detects fresh earnings or revenue report updates, computes a signed normalized surprise, and multiplies it by the inverse of a cash-conversion confirmation score built from conversion-cycle changes, income-quality changes, and receivables and inventory growth. The signal decays over six bars after the report rather than remaining active throughout the subsequent quarter.
factors.trading_idea: The economically relevant distinction is not simply whether an earnings surprise is large, but whether the headline surprise disagrees with contemporaneously available evidence on cash realization. Positive headline surprises accompanied by worsening conversion cycles, weak cash-flow quality, or elevated working-capital growth are prone to subsequent disappointment, while negative surprises accompanied by strong cash realization are more likely to be overly pessimistic. The prior result's negative IC supports trading this disagreement directly: higher disagreement should precede lower six-bar returns, with the effect concentrated immediately after a new report becomes available.

factors.name: Cash-Cycle Ambiguity Operating Fade
factors.description: The signal identifies fresh quarterly operating updates, combines cross-sectional improvements in DSO, inventory days, income quality, and revenue growth, and retains them for three bars. It is activated only when the preceding 20-bar return-sign entropy was high, sector-neutralized, and ranked so higher values represent stronger candidates for a negative six-bar correction.
factors.trading_idea: Fresh improvements in receivable days, inventory days, and cash-flow quality can be initially over-interpreted when the pre-disclosure price path has been directionally unresolved. Rather than treating the update as a broad quality premium, this factor isolates the subset released after high return-sign ambiguity, where investors are more likely to extrapolate a temporary working-capital improvement. The expected short-horizon effect remains corrective: stronger ambiguous operating improvements should precede lower subsequent returns.

factors.name: Fresh Coherent Revision Gap
factors.description: The signal ranks fresh standardized EPS/revenue estimate revisions that agree with a decayed history of prior revisions and exceed their recent industry-relative price response in volatility units. It is active only on estimate-update dates and uses a short response window suitable for a six-bar forecast.
factors.trading_idea: Analyst revisions should have the strongest six-bar drift when a new estimate change confirms a recent same-direction revision episode rather than representing an isolated update. The relevant short-horizon opportunity is the portion of a coherent revision that has not yet been absorbed by the stock's industry-relative return; stale episode exposure is deliberately removed. Cross-channel EPS and revenue agreement increases confidence that the revision reflects broad information discovery rather than a noisy single-field adjustment.

factors.name: Fundamental Peer Surprise Transmission Gap
factors.description: Create a rolling fundamental-neighbor basket from cross-sectional similarity in revenue growth, gross margin, operating margin, ROIC, and leverage. For each stock, compare its recent price response with the similarity-weighted recent earnings-surprise and revenue-surprise response of its peers; the factor is positive for firms underreacting to favorable peer news and negative for firms underreacting to unfavorable peer news, with a freshness decay based on recent changes in surprise fields.
factors.trading_idea: Earnings information from a reporting firm changes the implied outlook for economically similar firms, but cross-name transmission is delayed when the followers have not yet reported and have lower investor attention. A peer surprise that is corroborated by similar profitability, revenue growth, and operating-margin characteristics should therefore predict a catch-up move in the lagging firm's price. The hypothesis is rejected if peers with matched fundamentals do not react more than mismatched peers, or if the effect is equally strong after negative-quality or stale disclosures.

factors.name: Scheduled Flow Impact-Decay Reversal
factors.description: Measures signed idiosyncratic path efficiency over a ten-bar run, weighted by persistent and even relative-volume participation and by decaying recent price impact versus the earlier portion of the run. High values represent mature upward scheduled-flow episodes expected to reverse, while low values represent mature downward episodes expected to rebound.
factors.trading_idea: A persistent, same-signed idiosyncratic path accompanied by stable elevated participation can identify a gradually executed parent order, but the prior implementation incorrectly treated this state as continuation. At the six-bar horizon, the stronger interpretation is order completion: when abnormal participation remains elevated while the marginal price impact of the run decays, liquidity has increasingly absorbed the mechanical flow and its accumulated temporary impact is prone to unwind. The factor therefore retains the scheduled-execution mechanism but isolates its late, low-impact completion phase and predicts reversal rather than continuation.

factors.name: Sector Shock Distributed-Lag Catch-Up
factors.description: Builds a robust leave-one-out sector shock with broad-volume participation, removes its short-run autocorrelation, estimates each stock's trailing contemporaneous and 1-to-5-bar response coefficients, and ranks the delayed response expected from the current shock less the response already realized.
factors.trading_idea: Broad sector shocks can be incorporated contemporaneously by attention-dominant names while slower followers retain a predictable delayed response over the subsequent week. Rather than selecting a noisy single historical phase, the refined signal estimates a shrinkage-like distributed lag profile on leave-one-out sector-shock innovations and measures the response still unpaid after the stock's observed same-day reaction. The factor is active only when the shock is broadly volume-confirmed across sector peers, limiting the trade to plausible common-information events rather than idiosyncratic moves.

factors.name: Stabilized Convex Common-Shock Overshoot
factors.description: The signal fits a trailing intercept, linear, and signed-convex response of each stock to its leave-one-out industry return after standardizing the industry shock by its own trailing volatility. It ranks the volatility-normalized realized overshoot versus that fitted response, smoothly weighted by industry shock magnitude and directional coherence while excluding sparse industry groups.
factors.trading_idea: Broad, coherent industry shocks expose firms whose returns have nonlinear sensitivity to common moves, but a linear benchmark can misprice the size of that response. The prior implementation mixed a nonlinear fitted component with the stock's entire realized return, allowing ordinary linear industry exposure and idiosyncratic noise to dominate the gap. This refinement estimates the complete linear-plus-convex expected response using volatility-standardized leave-one-out industry shocks, then treats an excess realized response as an overreaction that should mean-revert; higher scores are therefore expected to precede lower 6-bar returns.

factors.name: Directed Lag-Graph Unpaid Response
factors.description: Builds a trailing within-industry directed graph from asymmetric one-day lagged residual-return correlations, routes current leader shocks to likely followers, and ranks the predicted follower response minus the follower's realized standardized return. The unpaid response is tilted toward names with low market-cap-normalized turnover.
factors.trading_idea: Common industry information is incorporated asynchronously when some stocks consistently lead and others follow rather than reacting simultaneously. A causal directed lead-lag graph identifies which peers historically transmit shocks into each follower; when current leader innovations imply a response that the follower has not yet made, the follower should catch up over the next several sessions. The effect should be strongest in low-turnover names, where sparse liquidity slows the price-discovery response rather than merely creating a generic contemporaneous peer-return gap.

factors.name: Shrunk Directed Liquidity Response Gap
factors.description: The signal estimates sparse within-industry one-day directed lead-lag weights from trailing industry-relative return innovations, routes current leader shocks to each follower, and measures the follower's unpaid response. It smooth-gates the gap by graph reliability and low industry-relative turnover before cross-sectionally ranking it.
factors.trading_idea: Industry information is incorporated asynchronously when historically leading stocks transmit idiosyncratic shocks to slower followers. A shrinkage-stabilized directed lag graph identifies only the asymmetric portion of those routes, while industry demeaning removes contemporaneous common news that can otherwise masquerade as directionality. The expected catch-up is strongest when the follower has structurally low industry-relative turnover, making an otherwise valid peer signal slower to incorporate.

factors.name: Return-Volume Recurrence Intensity Acceleration
factors.description: Uses continuous volatility-normalized return and relative-volume state weights, then compares short- versus medium-memory exponentially decayed recurrence intensity for each return direction. The signed, acceleration-gated state strength is cross-sectionally ranked, with unavailable early observations defensively assigned neutral signal.
factors.trading_idea: Directional, high-participation return states are evidence of an execution program when they recur more frequently than their own recent baseline. Rather than requiring exact revisits to brittle discrete return-volume bins, the refined signal estimates separate causal short- and medium-memory excitation intensities for positive and negative high-participation states. A current directional state is expected to continue over the next six bars when its same-direction recurrence intensity has recently accelerated, consistent with persistent order splitting and liquidity-taking before displayed liquidity replenishes.

factors.name: Directional Recurrence Saturation Completion
factors.description: The signal measures prior fast-versus-slow exponential recurrence intensity separately for positive and negative volume-weighted return states. It ranks the signed current state multiplied by its same-direction intensity level and acceleration; higher values represent increasingly saturated positive execution clusters and are expected to precede lower returns.
factors.trading_idea: Repeated high-participation directional return states still identify persistent execution activity, but the out-of-sample sign indicates that, at a six-bar horizon, accelerating recurrence is more often a late-stage saturation signal than an early-stage continuation signal. When same-direction marked events have recently become much more frequent than their slower baseline, liquidity-taking has likely concentrated into a near-complete execution episode, leaving depleted marginal demand and a subsequent reversal as liquidity replenishes. The refined implementation therefore preserves the recurrence-intensity mechanism while explicitly interpreting rapid intensity acceleration as execution completion rather than momentum.

factors.name: Sector Hawkes Late-Follower Compensator
factors.description: Construct signed abnormal-volume jump events from daily returns, intraday-range direction, and relative volume; estimate a causal exponentially decayed, leave-one-out sector event intensity as a discrete Hawkes-style compensator. Long stocks with a positive sector excitation intensity but unusually weak own signed response, and short the symmetric negative-excitation laggards, with the signal scaled down for weak current-ratio firms where apparent lagging may reflect financing distress rather than delayed assimilation.
factors.trading_idea: Information shocks and institutional reallocations often arrive as clustered, self-exciting sector-level order-flow events rather than as isolated stock moves. A stock that has not yet participated in a persistent same-signed sector volume-and-return burst is a likely late follower, especially when its balance-sheet liquidity provides capacity to absorb the repricing rather than forcing immediate deleveraging. The hypothesis is falsified if residual non-participation after a sector excitation predicts neither catch-up returns nor a reduction in the sector-relative price gap; the opposing side is short-horizon liquidity provision and benchmark-constrained traders who trade names independently while the sector shock diffuses.

factors.name: Signed Graph Curvature Residual Diffusion
factors.description: Compute sector-residual daily returns, build a rolling signed correlation graph, and estimate each ticker's local graph curvature from overlap and strength of its positive peer links. Score the negative of the current residual-return gap versus its curvature-weighted peer consensus, gated toward high-curvature communities and cross-sectionally ranked each date.
factors.trading_idea: A stock-specific residual move is more likely to converge when it occurs in a locally cohesive return-correlation network, where several strongly connected peers have not made the same move. Graph curvature distinguishes robust, redundant peer neighborhoods from fragile bridge-like relationships: a deviation inside a dense local community is more plausibly an incomplete information or order-flow diffusion than a genuine idiosyncratic repricing. The trade is against temporary liquidity providers and investors who transact a single name before systematically updating economically related holdings; the hypothesis is falsified if curvature-conditioned peer gaps do not mean-revert more strongly than equivalent gaps in weakly connected neighborhoods.

factors.name: Cross-Sectional Dispersion Regime Transfer
factors.description: Build a composite conservative-firm score from point-in-time freeCashFlowYield, roe, roic, incomeQuality, negative assetGrowth, negative debtGrowth, and negative sharesGrowth, standardized cross-sectionally within sector. Compute its cross-sectional dispersion and compare it with trailing realized return correlation to the sector or universe; emit the signed composite score only when dispersion is elevated and common return correlation is subdued, with a smooth continuous regime weight.
factors.trading_idea: The factor-timing paper motivates treating factor efficacy as regime dependent rather than mechanically constant. High cross-sectional dispersion in a slow-moving quality-minus-aggression score, combined with unusually low recent co-movement among its constituent stocks, indicates a stock-selection regime in which heterogeneous firm fundamentals can be priced independently; the opposite state indicates common-risk dominance and weak factor implementation. The trade is long firms with strong conservative-funding and cash-generation characteristics and short weak firms, but only when the dispersion-versus-correlation state is supportive. This is falsified if the conditional long-short spread is no stronger in high-dispersion, low-correlation regimes than in crowded, highly correlated regimes.

factors.name: Order-Flow Relaxation-Time Drift
factors.description: The signal estimates rolling lag-one persistence separately for log-volume surprises and absolute returns, then multiplies their persistence difference by a short recent signed return. It is high for positive recent moves supported by unusually persistent volume relative to volatility, and low for analogous negative moves or for volatility persistence unsupported by continued participation.
factors.trading_idea: Institutional execution programs produce a longer relaxation time in abnormal trading volume than in realised price volatility: volume remains serially persistent while the initial price response is partially obscured by temporary liquidity replenishment and benchmarked execution. When this persistence gap coincides with a recent directional price displacement, the displacement should continue over the next week as the latent program completes. The hypothesis is falsified if stocks with persistent volume shocks but rapidly decaying volatility do not exhibit directionally consistent subsequent returns; it may persist because identifying a latent execution schedule from noisy daily data is difficult and trading against it requires bearing adverse-selection and crowding risk.

factors.name: Persistent Liquidity Commonality De-Risking
factors.description: Computes each stock's trailing correlation between log Amihud-impact innovations and the robust cross-sectional median liquidity innovation. During positive five-day aggregate liquidity deterioration, it shorts high-commonality names and buys low-commonality names.
factors.trading_idea: Broad liquidity deterioration induces portfolio-level de-risking, and names whose own liquidity innovations reliably co-move with the market liquidity mode are more exposed to this forced-selling channel. The refined measure uses log changes in Amihud-style price impact, so commonality is measured on a multiplicative and scale-robust basis rather than being dominated by dollar-volume levels or volatility. The signal is active only when aggregate liquidity has deteriorated persistently over the prior week, a state more likely to remain relevant over the fixed 6-bar forecast horizon than a single-day shock.

factors.name: Intraday Supply-Curve Overshoot Reversal
factors.description: Measures intraday range after square-root relative-volume adjustment, standardizes its innovation against a trailing robust baseline, retains stock-specific positive fragility shocks, and takes the opposite of the close-location direction. High values represent downside intraday overshoots expected to rebound, while low values represent upside overshoots expected to fade.
factors.trading_idea: A disproportionately large intraday range produced without unusually high participation indicates that the available liquidity supply curve was thin: a small amount of directional trading traversed a large price interval. The evaluation evidence indicates that these directional excursions reverse rather than persist, with the strongest effect expected when the range shock is idiosyncratic to the stock rather than a sector-wide volatility event. The refined factor therefore fades extreme-close, low-participation range overshoots while removing overnight-gap and broad sector components.

factors.name: Thin-Side Square-Root Impact Impulse
factors.description: The signal measures a signed, volatility-normalised return multiplied by the positive surprise in square-root price impact, where impact is abnormal absolute return per square root of relative dollar volume. It cross-sectionally ranks only confirmed directional moves occurring in an unusually thin liquidity state.
factors.trading_idea: A price move that is unusually large relative to both the stock's recent volatility and the square root of its contemporaneous traded dollar volume indicates a temporarily thin side of the latent order book. When the move closes in its own direction, the imbalance is more likely to reflect persistent execution demand than a transitory intraday excursion, so the directional impulse should continue over the next several daily bars. Normalising first by trailing volatility and then by the stock's own impact history isolates liquidity fragility rather than simply rewarding volatile names.

factors.name: Completed Marked Arrival Absorption Reversal
factors.description: Ranks the signed direction of a recently elevated, now-cooling volume-marked arrival burst, gated by directional coherence and price impact efficiency below the name's trailing median. High values are completed absorbed buy-pressure episodes and are expected to precede weaker returns; low values are analogous sell-pressure episodes expected to rebound.
factors.trading_idea: Directional, unusual volume-marked arrivals that produce little price displacement are more consistent with liquidity-provider absorption than with an information shock still awaiting assimilation. The prior version treated this muted-impact state as unabsorbed demand that should continue, but the consistently negative realized IC indicates that it more often identifies temporary execution pressure. Reversal should be most timely at six bars once the marked-arrival intensity has begun to cool after a coherent burst, indicating that the parent-order impulse is completing while dealer inventory and transient impact unwind.

factors.name: Report Assimilation Release Continuation
factors.description: Ranks surprise-direction continuation after a newly detected EPS report, weighting normalized surprise magnitude, muted initial response per unit surprise, lagged signed abnormal volume, and a joint range-volume release score. It is active only two to five bars after the report.
factors.trading_idea: The original fade's negative realized IC implies that post-report surprise-direction pressure remains informative at the six-bar horizon even after range and volume begin to normalize: the apparent release is more consistent with liquidity becoming available for informed demand to transmit than with trader exhaustion. A large EPS surprise with a muted initial price response leaves an assimilation deficit, while subsequent surprise-aligned abnormal trading identifies that the residual order flow is directional rather than a one-bar announcement shock. The factor therefore follows, rather than fades, this pressure only during a jointly stressed-then-cooling liquidity state.

factors.name: Idiosyncratic Thin-Side Vacuum Reversal
factors.description: Computes a market-residual return scaled by trailing idiosyncratic volatility, identifies robustly unusual displacement per square root of relative dollar volume, and fades the signed impulse when dollar-volume participation is low. Cross-sectional ranking makes high values correspond to expected rebound after a thin-side excursion.
factors.trading_idea: An abnormally large idiosyncratic price displacement on unusually little dollar volume is more consistent with a temporary vacancy on one side of the latent book than with durable informed execution demand. The prior implementation treated close-direction agreement as confirmation of continuation, but the observed negative IC indicates that daily-bar low-participation impulses are predominantly liquidity-vacuum overshoots. The refined signal therefore isolates stock-specific, robustly abnormal square-root impact and takes the opposite side of the impulse, with stronger exposure only when participation is distinctly below the stock's own normal level.

factors.name: Shrunk Sector Mode Follower Relay
factors.description: Computes a shrunk trailing sector correlation mode from standardized log-range innovations, measures its localization and eigengap confidence, and scores low-loading names whose short return lags the leave-one-out mode-weighted sector impulse. The final signal is cross-sectionally ranked each day.
factors.trading_idea: Localized synchronization in sector volatility innovations can identify a connected pocket experiencing a common information or constrained-flow shock. The economically delayed recipients are not necessarily the largest eigenmode-loading names; they are the lower-loading sector members whose recent return has not yet caught up with the leave-one-out directional move of the localized pocket. Shrinking the correlation matrix and using a continuous eigengap-confidence weight reduces instability from small sector groups and noisy realized-range correlations while retaining the original directional relay mechanism.

factors.name: Fresh Cash-Funded Upgrade Wedge
factors.description: The signal detects a fresh 20-bar normalized EPS-estimate upgrade, then scales it by a cross-sectional funding-quality wedge: free-cash-flow yield minus net-stock-issuance intensity. Non-upgrades and observations with unavailable inputs are assigned a neutral score.
factors.trading_idea: Analyst upgrades should be most informative immediately after they occur, but their credibility depends on whether the firm can fund the implied growth internally. A fresh EPS-consensus upgrade backed by strong free-cash-flow generation and little net equity issuance is more likely to persist, whereas an otherwise similar upgrade at an equity-financed firm is vulnerable to delayed recognition of dilution. This refinement removes the prior signal's sign-confounding interaction, eliminates slow price-confirmation branches, and treats financing quality as a gate on fresh upgrades rather than as a standalone directional forecast.

factors.name: Tail Survival Capacity Impedance
factors.description: On aligned quarterly revenue-surprise and operating-cash-flow-growth updates, the signal ranks the signed joint innovation scaled by trailing realized volatility, prior revenue/cash-flow downside-tail asymmetry, and muted current volume versus its recent median. It is active only for firms with a pre-existing asymmetric downside-tail state and a fresh aligned fundamental update.
factors.trading_idea: A favorable joint revenue-surprise and operating-cash-flow update is especially informative when a firm has historically exhibited asymmetric downside fundamental tails: the feared disaster state has failed to occur. That survival information should drift most strongly when the shock is large relative to recent realized volatility and release-day participation is muted, because risk-budget-constrained investors and execution desks cannot immediately scale into the position. The interaction has edge beyond Parent B's tail state alone because it identifies when tail repricing is operationally delayed, and beyond Parent A's capacity mismatch alone because it restricts attention to shocks that resolve a pre-existing disaster-risk narrative.

factors.name: Fresh Accounting-Confirmed Surprise
factors.description: The signal ranks fresh estimate-normalized earnings and revenue surprises, scaled up when gross margin, operating-cash-flow margin, and working-capital intensity move in the same sustainable direction. It subtracts the contemporaneous cross-sectional price reaction and carries the event for only two additional bars.
factors.trading_idea: Earnings and revenue surprises should drift when the reported headline is corroborated by contemporaneous improvements in unit economics, cash profitability, and working-capital discipline. The prior implementation over-expanded the event definition: an update in any accounting field could repeatedly reactivate a stale surprise, creating noisy and overfit event histories. This refinement fires only on a fresh headline-surprise update, normalizes surprises by their relevant consensus estimate, and retains the same underreaction mechanism by discounting names whose immediate price response has already incorporated the news.

factors.name: Partial-Graph Peer Innovation Catch-Up
factors.description: Compute daily residual returns by removing equal-weight sector returns, estimate a rolling sparse precision/partial-correlation graph from approximately 60 trailing residual-return observations, and form each stock's peer innovation as the edge-weighted mean of its connected peers' recent 2-3 day residual returns excluding itself. Score stocks by the gap between this peer innovation and their own recent residual return, retaining only nodes with stable positive graph links and cross-sectionally ranking the resulting catch-up signal.
factors.trading_idea: Constructing peer groups from marginal correlations can confuse common sector beta with economically meaningful transmission links; a sparse partial-correlation graph instead identifies names whose returns remain conditionally connected after broad-market and sector effects. When a stock has not yet reflected a recent, coherent innovation among its conditionally linked peers, it should catch up over the next week as relative-value desks and sector specialists propagate the information. The other side is passive benchmark flow and investors who react to visible sector moves but do not continuously update a sparse conditional peer map; the edge should disappear if partial-graph neighbor innovations no longer predict residual forward returns after controlling for ordinary industry momentum. This adapts the graph-clustering statistical-arbitrage mechanism of the source paper while replacing cluster-average reversal with a directed conditional-information diffusion signal.

factors.name: Quality-Regime Issuer Distribution
factors.description: Computes industry-relative issuance/dilution and a completed turnover-cooling/near-high state, then weights it by the negative of sector-relative quality-value exposure. The score is active only when a lagged self-financing quality-value sleeve has positive reward-to-dispersion and positive return breadth.
factors.trading_idea: Issuer supply that appears absorbed near recent highs is not necessarily bullish: in a persistent quality-value leadership regime, investors are more discriminating about dilution and weak-fundamental issuers can remain temporarily supported while distribution completes. The child targets high-supply, turnover-cooling issuers specifically when they are expensive and low quality relative to their sector and when the quality-value sleeve has broad positive realized breadth. This interaction carries edge because the quality-value state distinguishes credible capital raising from delayed repricing of low-quality dilution, while the supply-absorption pattern identifies the short-horizon timing of that repricing.

factors.name: Fresh Expectation Delivery
factors.description: Ranks a compact expectation-delivery score combining revenue growth, free-cash-flow yield, cash-flow quality, dilution, and sales valuation. The cross-sectional score is scaled by an exponentially decaying indicator of how recently any of those reported fundamentals changed.
factors.trading_idea: Investors extrapolate revenue growth and high-sales narratives, but the distinction between growth that is cash-backed and growth supported by dilution, weak cash conversion, or expensive valuation becomes most decision-relevant when new quarterly information is released. The original persistent-premium timing overlay is replaced by a simpler and more causal disclosure-recency condition: slow institutional assimilation should be strongest immediately after the market receives updated evidence of delivery quality. Firms with fresh, cash-backed growth should outperform fresh narrative-dependent growth over the following six trading days.

factors.name: Growth-Expectation Convexity Break
factors.description: Compute sector-relative valuation richness from psRatio, combine it with the acceleration of recent returns (recent short-window return minus prior-window return), and multiply by the negative of quarter-over-quarter changes in revenueGrowth and operatingMargin. Cross-sectionally rank the resulting signed expectation-break score, with high values indicating likely over-extrapolation and negative expected six-bar returns.
factors.trading_idea: Investors often extrapolate a rapidly accelerating price path most aggressively when a high-valuation growth stock has just stopped delivering incremental improvement in its underlying growth or profitability. The signal shorts names with convex recent price appreciation, expensive sector-relative sales valuation, and decelerating reported revenue growth or operating-margin change; it buys the converse. The inefficiency should persist because narrative-driven investors and benchmarked growth managers react to the level of growth and the visible price trend, while the more important second derivative of operating delivery is sparse, quarterly, and costly to trade against. The idea is falsified if post-signal returns continue to reward price convexity equally among firms with worsening versus improving fundamental acceleration.

factors.name: Fresh Growth-Expectation Break
factors.description: The factor ranks stocks with simultaneously rich sector-relative sales valuation, volatility-normalized price-path acceleration, and a fresh trailing 12-bar deterioration in reported revenue growth or operating margin. Fundamental deterioration is measured only on actual point-in-time disclosure changes and then retained briefly as a decaying event state.
factors.trading_idea: Narrative-driven investors can continue extrapolating a strong, accelerating price path immediately after a growth company reports a fresh deterioration in revenue-growth or margin momentum. The relevant implementation is a short-lived post-disclosure state rather than a continuously active quarterly level signal: rich sector-relative valuation and price convexity matter most when the underlying delivery break has just become public. High signal values identify the most crowded over-extrapolation states and should precede lower six-bar returns.

factors.name: Fundamental-Contradicted Momentum Extrapolation
factors.description: Compute a robust 60-day price trend excluding the most recent 5 days, then multiply its negative by a cross-sectional fundamental deterioration composite built from quarter-over-quarter changes in epsEstimate, revenueEstimate, operatingMargin, freeCashFlow, and ROIC. Apply stronger weights where valuation is demanding, using percentile ranks of psRatio and evToSales, and neutralize the final score within sector.
factors.trading_idea: Investors tend to extrapolate recent price leadership, particularly in glamour firms, even when newly available operating evidence contradicts the narrative. The signal targets stocks whose medium-term price trend is strong but whose cross-sectional fundamental revision impulse is deteriorating, and vice versa for short candidates; the expected payoff is a correction as slower-moving fundamental allocators and earnings-aware investors reassess the trend. This is falsified if trend-following returns remain strongest precisely among firms with adverse revenue, margin, cash-flow, and estimate changes, rather than weakening or reversing. It is linked to the supplied factor-timing paper's emphasis on conditional factor payoffs: momentum's premium should depend on the fundamental state rather than be treated as unconditional.

factors.name: Fresh Downside Pressure
factors.description: Computes volume-surprise-weighted signed returns, compares the latest 5-bar pressure to the preceding 20-bar state, and scales the deterioration by trailing signed-pressure volatility. High values indicate a fresh, abnormal downside-pressure cluster.
factors.trading_idea: A new cluster of negative returns on unusually high volume is a daily-bar proxy for asymmetric sell-order excitation: stop-losses, deleveraging, and liquidity withdrawal can propagate selling beyond the initial shock. The relevant state is fresh downside pressure relative to the name's own recent signed return-volume process, rather than a heavily parameterized estimate of separate buy and sell kernels. Names with the strongest fresh downside-pressure shocks should have lower returns over the next six trading days as the sell sequence continues.

factors.name: Cashflow-Strain Idiosyncratic Overshoot
factors.description: The signal multiplies a pre-event-normalized sector-residual downside-return innovation by a sector-relative composite of recent deterioration in cash conversion, operating margin, and interest coverage. It ranks names with both an idiosyncratic downside shock and worsening operating-financing resilience.
factors.trading_idea: Downside overshoots should be most reversible when selling is idiosyncratic rather than a sector-wide repricing, because the price move is more likely to reflect a temporary withdrawal of risk-bearing capacity. The relevant fragility is not a static low-quality label, but a recently deteriorating ability to convert revenue into cash, maintain margins, and service debt. Firms with this worsening operating-financing cushion can exhibit nonlinear panic repricing after an unusually large sector-relative loss, followed by a six-bar rebound once forced selling pressure dissipates.

factors.name: Tail-Survival Forced-Flow Reversal
factors.description: Ranks the interaction of lagged asymmetric downside fundamental-tail exposure, fresh concordant revenue-surprise/cash-flow-growth news, and fresh abnormal-volume downside pressure. Positive survival news accompanied by unusually fresh selling receives the highest score, while negative confirmation under the same execution state receives the lowest score.
factors.trading_idea: A favorable quarterly survival confirmation is most valuable when it arrives for firms with a prior history of asymmetric fundamental downside risk, because it removes a disaster discount that had made holders prone to defensive liquidation. If such confirmation coincides with fresh abnormal-volume downside pressure, the selling is more likely scheduled deleveraging or liquidity-driven execution than new adverse information, creating a temporary price concession and six-bar rebound; conversely, adverse confirmation plus the same pressure identifies genuine deterioration. Neither parent isolates this distinction: the fundamental signal does not observe whether its repricing is being distorted by forced execution, while the price-volume signal alone cannot distinguish informed selling from selling against verified survival.

factors.name: Superlinear Downside Variance Relaxation
factors.description: Using causal rolling daily OHLCV data, estimate downside realized-range innovations and their subsequent decay conditional on shock magnitude, fitting a stock-specific nonlinear relationship between shock size and future variance relaxation. Cross-sectionally rank the current downside shock multiplied by the estimated superlinear relaxation propensity, with volume used to distinguish liquidation-like shocks from informational high-participation moves.
factors.trading_idea: Negative-return volatility shocks are not symmetric with positive shocks: sell-side liquidity can evaporate during declines, but forced selling and hedging demand eventually exhaust, creating a nonlinear acceleration in volatility mean reversion. The signal identifies stocks whose own historical large downside range/volume shocks have decayed materially faster than ordinary shocks, then buys current downside dislocations where this exhaustion pattern is active and shorts names whose downside variance historically remains persistent. The hypothesis is falsified if post-shock return reversal is no stronger for names with a steep magnitude-dependent volatility-decay curve than for names with linear or persistent decay; limits to arbitrage arise because trading into a high-volatility selloff is capital- and risk-budget intensive.

factors.name: Downside Excitation Fragility Acceleration
factors.description: The signal constructs marked downside events from return shocks, abnormal volume, and abnormal intraday range, then measures the gap between fast and slow exponentially weighted event intensities. It upweights this acceleration by a cross-sectional financial-fragility score based on profitability, liquidity, and leverage.
factors.trading_idea: Forced selling is not fully exhausted over six daily bars when a downside shock arrives with an unusually rapid acceleration in downside-event intensity, elevated trading activity, and expanded range. The evaluation evidence indicates that the near-term effect is continuation rather than an immediate quality-led snapback, so financial quality is used as an information-content gate: the same cascade is more likely to persist in financially fragile firms, where deleveraging and financing risk make selling more fundamental. High values therefore identify fragile names with freshly accelerating downside excitation and should precede lower six-bar returns.

factors.name: Fragile Downside Persistence Exhaustion
factors.description: The signal combines a fresh downside-range innovation with a fast-versus-slow downside-intensity persistence measure and a defensive leverage/interest-coverage fragility score. It ranks names by likely forced-selling exhaustion, with high values expected to precede positive six-bar returns.
factors.trading_idea: Persistent downside volatility still identifies the same endogenous de-risking mechanism: negative price excursions induce further selling through risk controls, margin pressure, and constrained dealer balance sheets. The prior implementation's negative six-bar IC indicates that, at this horizon, the economically relevant tradable effect is the exhaustion of that selling pressure rather than further continuation. Stocks with a fresh adverse excursion embedded in a persistent downside-volatility cluster, especially financially fragile firms, should therefore experience the strongest subsequent rebound.

factors.name: Resilient Downside Excitation Cooling
factors.description: The signal ranks names with unusually elevated medium-horizon downside excitation, a positive fast-to-slow cooling gap, and lingering downside-associated abnormal-volume execution. Cash liquidity and low leverage provide a modest resilience gate, while robust return scaling and a long-memory baseline reduce sensitivity to volatility level and isolated jumps.
factors.trading_idea: Clustered downside returns can arise from self-exciting deleveraging and sell-program activity rather than a single isolated repricing. The evaluation indicates that a fading fast downside rate while medium-memory downside pressure remains high is, over six days, more often the orderly cooling phase of an unfinished liquidation program than its terminal exhaustion; the expected direction should therefore be negative. A balance-sheet liquidity buffer is retained as a mild conditioning variable because it distinguishes protracted flow-driven selling from immediate financing-distress repricing, rather than overwhelming the market-based cascade evidence.

factors.name: Prompt Cooling Thin-Traversal Reversal
factors.description: Ranks the negative recent idiosyncratic displacement of stocks with a recent thin-liquidity traversal, weighting it by immediate cooling, directional coherence, gap continuity, and low cross-sectional stress breadth. The use of smooth cooling and breadth weights replaces discrete delayed episode confirmation with a more timely six-bar reversal trigger.
factors.trading_idea: A large, coherent intraday traversal through unusually thin liquidity can reflect a temporary liquidity vacuum or completed forced order flow rather than durable information. The reversal should begin promptly once current range-per-participation normalizes below a recent stress peak, so the implementation measures cooling at the current bar rather than waiting through a fixed post-event delay. The effect is strongest when the preceding traversal direction agrees with the idiosyncratic displacement and when the stress was narrow rather than a broad market liquidity withdrawal.

factors.name: Asymmetric Overnight Range Wedge Rebound
factors.description: Computes a GJR-style downside conditional-variance excess from close-to-close log returns versus a matched Rogers-Satchell intraday range forecast. The positive wedge is gated by fresh standardized negative overnight or close-to-close shocks, neutralized within sector, and cross-sectionally ranked.
factors.trading_idea: Bad-news shocks raise close-to-close conditional volatility more than symmetric or intraday range estimators, especially when a negative overnight jump is not represented by the subsequent intraday path. The prior implementation's realized sign is opposite its stated delayed-de-risking interpretation: a large downside return-versus-range wedge has historically preceded stronger, not weaker, returns. The refined hypothesis is that such wedges identify an already concentrated asymmetric risk repricing and forced-sale episode, after which the residual range-model underreaction is followed by a short-horizon rebound; sector-neutralization isolates idiosyncratic rather than broad market stress.

factors.name: Financing-Gated Downside Polarity
factors.description: Computes a trailing, sector-residual downside-excitation state and interacts it with positive analyst revisions weighted by financing credibility. High values identify cash-backed upgrades experiencing an idiosyncratic selloff; low values identify externally funded upgrades whose downside shock is likely to propagate.
factors.trading_idea: An idiosyncratic downside excitation is ambiguous by itself: it can be a temporary liquidity overshoot or the start of a reassessment of fragile growth. The financing-credibility state resolves that ambiguity: sell externally financed upgrades after a clustered sector-relative downside shock, because revision-following capital withdraws when dilution and weak cash support become salient; buy cash-supported upgrades after the same shock, where selling is more likely a temporary capacity-driven overshoot. Neither parent has this polarity distinction alone: the shock factor lacks a way to separate information cascades from reversible selling, while the revision-financing wedge becomes timely only when downside order-flow stress forces investors to process funding quality.

factors.name: Downside Reflexive Probe Persistence
factors.description: The signal combines fast downside-versus-upside semivariance asymmetry, its increase relative to a slower baseline, positive abnormal volume participation, and a trailing volume-weighted measure of closes recovering from downside intrabar probes. High values identify persistent, high-participation false-absorption states and are expected to precede lower six-bar returns.
factors.trading_idea: Negative shocks can generate self-exciting selling pressure: repeated downside excursions attract temporary liquidity, allowing closes to recover from intrabar lows without resolving the underlying inventory imbalance. The prior implementation's consistently negative IC indicates that apparent absorption is more often deceptive than bullish at the fixed six-bar horizon: high downside-variance asymmetry combined with elevated participation and repeated recovered probes should precede further weakness. This refinement emphasizes a fresh acceleration in downside asymmetry and persistence of recovered downside probes, rather than allowing below-normal volume or a single noisy candle to determine the state.

factors.name: Scheduled Downside Cooling Drift
factors.description: Measures a slow, broad downside-volume impulse, its recent cooling, directional coherence, and the serial regularity of downside pressure. High values identify orderly sell programs whose cooling historically behaves as adverse-information drift rather than mechanical-rebound completion.
factors.trading_idea: A broad, regular, high-volume downside program is more likely to reflect persistent information-motivated supply than a one-off liquidity shock. The prior rebound interpretation is contradicted by the data: when such a program cools, the reduction in observed selling appears to be a temporary execution pause or partial completion while adverse information continues to be incorporated. Therefore, names with the clearest broad and predictable sell schedule followed by cooling should underperform over the next six bars.

factors.name: Unpaid Downside Tail-Bridge Diffusion
factors.description: Build a rolling residual-return network within sector using 60-day demeaned returns, with each edge weighted by excess lower-tail co-exceedance probability relative to upper-tail co-exceedance probability. For each stock, compute a tail-bridge score from its connectivity across distinct local correlation communities, then multiply this by the negative residual gap between its one-day return and the tail-connectivity-weighted return of shocked peers; scale the short signal upward for high debtToEquity and low currentRatio, and cross-sectionally rank.
factors.trading_idea: A stock that is a bridge between otherwise distinct downside-tail communities can transmit stress when correlated peers suffer simultaneous extreme losses, even if its own initial reaction is muted. This reflects asymmetric excitation of downward orders: deleveraging, risk-limit reductions, and basket hedging propagate more reliably through left-tail dependence than through ordinary return correlation. The factor shorts bridge names with an underreacted contemporaneous response to a peer-tail shock, especially when leverage is high and liquidity buffers are weak; the hypothesis is falsified if these names do not subsequently converge to the stressed-neighbor return over the next six sessions. The graph-clustering motivation follows the paper's use of residual-return relationships, but replaces unconditional correlation with asymmetric lower-tail connectivity to target crisis transmission rather than generic pair convergence.

factors.name: Robust Tail Equity-Supply Reversal
factors.description: Computes each stock's largest positive standardized daily return over a recent trailing interval, then interacts its cross-sectional tail rank with an available-only rank of net equity issuance scaled by market capitalization and share-count growth. The returned score is inverted so higher values identify names expected to outperform the issuance-backed lottery-tail candidates.
factors.trading_idea: Lottery-like overpricing is most likely after a stock has recently delivered an unusually large upside realization relative to its own normal volatility, because investors extrapolate a positively skewed payoff distribution. The reversal should be sharper when the firm is simultaneously a net supplier of equity: issuance relative to market value or an expanding share count provides a cleaner, informed counterweight to speculative demand. This refinement uses a single robust extreme-return statistic and scale-free, available-only dilution measures rather than multiple correlated tail and supply branches.

factors.name: Cash-Cycle Replenishment Rebound
factors.description: The signal ranks working-capital intensity within industry and activates it only when a stock has an idiosyncratic, high-relative-volume downside impulse in the prior three bars followed by a positive idiosyncratic rebound. It uses one stable one-month normalization window and removes industry-level return moves before identifying sell pressure.
factors.trading_idea: Cash-cycle-intensive firms are especially prone to liquidity-motivated de-risking when an idiosyncratic high-participation selloff occurs, because investors are sensitive to the financing burden of receivables and inventory. The out-of-sample sign indicates that a prompt rebound after this sell-pressure episode more often marks completion of a scheduled or forced sell program and replenishment of displayed liquidity, rather than delayed fundamental deterioration. Thus, high working-capital-intensity names whose idiosyncratic downside shock is followed by an immediate rebound should continue to outperform over the next six bars.

factors.name: Idiosyncratic Tail-Resilience Absorption Repair
factors.description: Ranks a robust idiosyncratic sell-backlog completion event: abnormal intraday downside excursion, high participation, and strong close-from-low recovery. It conditions that event on fresh quarterly lower-tail resilience in operating-cash-flow-to-assets and gross margin plus robust value support.
factors.trading_idea: A sequence of idiosyncratic downside moves followed by a high-volume lower-wick recovery is more consistent with the exhaustion of a scheduled sell program than with broad market repricing. The signal is strongest when the issuer has repeatedly preserved operating-cash-flow efficiency and gross margins through its own prior adverse reporting outcomes, and is still cheaply valued, making transient flow-driven distress more likely to repair. Removing the contemporaneous sector return isolates name-specific execution pressure from sector-wide information shocks that should not be mechanically faded.

factors.name: Report-Clock Tail Contagion Derisking
factors.description: The signal constructs sector leave-one-out beta residuals, measures excess lower-tail co-exceedance connectivity, and identifies tail-central names whose peers recently sold off more than they did. It ranks this short-side vulnerability only when the stock is near an inferred reporting clock and its Parkinson range volatility is accelerating.
factors.trading_idea: A beta-residual tail-loss in economically connected sector peers is most likely to transmit to an initially resilient stock when it occurs immediately before that stock's recurring reporting or estimate-update window. Near that information-resolution clock, volatility acceleration signals thinner effective liquidity and more urgent informed-trader or hedger execution, so the peer-tail gap is less likely to be absorbed and more likely to close within the fixed six-bar horizon. Parent A identifies who is exposed to delayed common-shock contagion, while Parent B identifies when price formation is unusually sensitive; neither alone distinguishes a harmless peer selloff from a report-clock liquidity-constrained de-risking episode.

factors.name: Anticipated Report Peer-Tail Impact
factors.description: The signal measures a stock's three-day beta-residual resilience versus its leave-one-out sector peers' downside residual shock, gated by proximity to its inferred recurring earnings-report clock and by a recent Amihud-style price-impact acceleration. High values identify resilient names likely to catch down as peer-tail risk transmits.
factors.trading_idea: A stock that remains comparatively resilient while its sector peers suffer a concentrated idiosyncratic downside shock is exposed to delayed de-risking rather than necessarily demonstrating fundamental strength. This transmission is most acute immediately before the stock's empirically inferred reporting window, when scheduled information resolution and execution demand make liquidity providers less willing to absorb sector risk. Elevated short-run price impact is used as the liquidity-sensitivity gate, replacing a noisy range-only volatility trigger.

factors.name: Signed Volume-Clock Schedule Continuation
factors.description: The signal estimates a trailing regression of cumulative sector-residual, volatility-scaled returns on cumulative close-location-signed relative volume. It ranks the signed slope only when the path has high fit, persistent directional flow, elevated recent participation, and recent return confirmation.
factors.trading_idea: Large informed orders are commonly sliced across days, creating persistent close-location-implied signed flow whose cumulative price response is smooth in volume time. The relevant six-bar continuation state is not merely a historical smooth path: the schedule must remain directionally active in the most recent week, occur at elevated participation, and be distinct from a broad sector move. A positive signed impact slope with high volume-clock fit indicates continuing buy-program demand, while a negative slope indicates continuing sell-program supply.

factors.name: Calendar-Phase Metaorder Impact Deficit
factors.description: Estimate daily signed participation as relative volume times normalized close location within the bar, then measure directional persistence and spectral concentration at a five-bar calendar frequency over a trailing window. Go long (short) names with coherent positive (negative) scheduled flow whose cumulative return is small relative to their accumulated signed participation, cross-sectionally normalizing the resulting impact-deficit score.
factors.trading_idea: Large informed or benchmarked investors commonly split parent orders into regular daily execution schedules to control footprint and liquidity cost. A persistent directional, volume-weighted close-location flow with statistically concentrated weekly-calendar phase, but unusually muted cumulative price impact, indicates that available depth has temporarily absorbed rather than completed the parent order; the residual schedule should continue to exert pressure over the next week. The hypothesis is falsified if phase-coherent low-impact flows reverse as often as irregular flows, implying that the pattern reflects routine liquidity provision rather than unfinished execution.

factors.name: Persistent Participation Pressure
factors.description: Computes volume surprises relative to each stock's trailing log-volume distribution, multiplies positive abnormal participation by signed close-location and normalized range impact, then exponentially aggregates the pressure. A directional-consistency ratio downweights isolated or alternating pressure observations before cross-sectional ranking.
factors.trading_idea: Execution algorithms spread metaorders across several sessions, producing repeated abnormal participation accompanied by closes near one side of the daily range. Unlike a stock-specific transition table, persistent signed abnormal participation is a direct and more stable proxy for unresolved inventory demand. The signal is strongest when recent participation-pressure observations agree in sign, indicating an active schedule rather than a one-bar liquidity shock; positive pressure should precede positive six-bar returns.

factors.name: Novel Surprise Absorption Drift
factors.description: The factor standardizes fresh EPS and revenue surprises by each firm's trailing history of announced surprises, then selects surprises with low one-day volatility-scaled idiosyncratic price impact despite elevated relative volume. Fresh event signals are carried for three bars with a deterministic decay and cross-sectionally ranked.
factors.trading_idea: Earnings information should continue to diffuse when a surprise is unusually large relative to the issuer's own prior surprise history but its immediate idiosyncratic price response is muted. Muted displacement accompanied by normal-to-high trading activity is interpreted as passive-liquidity absorption or constrained rebalancing, rather than simple absence of investor attention. The signal carries the surprise direction forward for a short post-release assimilation interval, targeting delayed incorporation at the fixed six-bar horizon.

factors.name: Industry Turnover-Gated Idiosyncratic Repair
factors.description: The signal fades a stock's volatility-normalized daily residual return versus a leave-one-out industry peer return, but only in proportion to how far its dollar turnover is below its own trailing median. Sector peers provide a fallback where an industry has insufficient contemporaneous constituents.
factors.trading_idea: A large one-day return departure from a stock's leave-one-out industry basket is more likely to be a transient inventory or liquidity displacement when it occurs on abnormally low turnover relative to the stock's own trading capacity. Unlike an information-driven move, a shallow-participation deviation has not attracted sufficient capital to validate the repricing and should be repaired as liquidity providers and relative-value traders replenish inventory. Using stable industry peers and a direct market-cap-scaled turnover gate avoids the unstable graph membership and multi-stage spectral fitting that likely delayed the parent signal beyond the fixed six-bar horizon.

factors.name: Latent Impact Absorption Persistence
factors.description: For each stock, estimate a causal rolling impact model relating signed intrabar return (close/open minus one) to signed relative volume, with an industry leave-one-out signed-flow control. Score the current directional-flow residual when observed price impact is materially below model-implied impact, multiplied by the recent persistence of same-signed flow; positive values indicate buy-flow absorption and negative values sell-flow absorption.
factors.trading_idea: A large directional volume shock that produces unusually little contemporaneous price movement indicates that liquidity providers or patient counterparties are absorbing a one-sided metaorder rather than that the demand has cleared. If the directional flow remains persistent over several bars, the absorbed inventory and incomplete information incorporation should generate subsequent price continuation as market depth is replenished and the latent demand is repriced. The signal should fail when muted price response is caused by genuinely symmetric two-sided trading, so it is explicitly gated on persistent signed flow and elevated relative volume.

factors.name: Fractional Propagator Flow-Debt Reversal
factors.description: For each stock, construct signed participation from volume times the bar's close-location value, normalize it by rolling volume and range, and convolve recent flow with a causal fractional-decay kernel. Estimate a rolling industry-neutral return impact loading, then score the negative residual between observed industry-neutral cumulative price displacement and the displacement implied by inherited propagator flow; high positive scores identify overextended upward impact expected to mean-revert, and vice versa.
factors.trading_idea: Daily signed volume inferred from close location within the bar contains a noisy proxy for persistent directional execution. Under a concave, slowly decaying impact propagator, an unusually large price move relative to the still-active impact implied by recent signed participation represents excess trading pressure rather than new information; inventory-averse liquidity suppliers and arbitrageurs should subsequently unwind that residual over the next week. The signal should fail if price dislocations above propagator-implied impact continue to drift in the same direction, indicating that the apparent flow is predominantly informed rather than transient. This is related to the competitive statistical-arbitrage motivation in the supplied graph-clustering paper, but uses causal impact-deconvolution rather than a simple peer-return deviation.

factors.name: Sector-Relative Opening Auction Rejection
factors.description: Computes a robust own-history and sector-relative opening-gap surprise, then signs a score toward reversal when the bar both probes and closes materially against that gap direction. Relative volume continuously upweights rejected auctions with greater inventory-transfer evidence.
factors.trading_idea: An opening move that is exceptional for the stock after removing its sector's contemporaneous auction move, but is subsequently traversed back through the open and closes adversely, is evidence that one-sided opening liquidity was consumed rather than that information was accepted into the price. Unusually high participation makes this rejection more diagnostic of temporary inventory transfer: the auction has attracted sufficient opposing flow to reveal that the initial price was not sustainable. The previous sign conflict was effectively non-informative because the cooling gate produced a nearly all-zero cross-section; this refinement preserves the reversal direction while measuring completed rejection directly and using volume as a continuous confidence weight.

factors.name: Decelerating Execution-Debt Reversal
factors.description: The signal measures industry-neutral price displacement relative to its own volatility, then fades it only when an eight-bar signed participation debt is coherent, aligned with the move, and recent signed participation is weaker than the preceding execution block. Participation is inferred from industry-neutral return direction and robust relative volume.
factors.trading_idea: Persistent, one-sided volume-weighted trading can create a temporary inventory and price-impact debt as liquidity suppliers intermediate a metaorder. The effect should reverse over the next week specifically when the prior directional execution remains coherent but its intensity is decelerating, which is more consistent with completion of mechanical trading than with continuing informed demand. Conditioning on deceleration and directional agreement between price displacement and accumulated flow avoids fading active, information-driven trends.
